source_read: PDF (journal 'article in press' version, pages numbered 1-8), all pages read; Fig. 1 (p. 4) and Tables 1-3 (p. 5) checked on rendered pages; supplementary tables 1-3 not seen.

claims.overstatement: None material for this source. One wording point: 'read by site staff' is not in the paper, which describes the service's procedure (2-3 mg analysed by FTIR, then dissolved in water, strip added, one combined result recorded) but never says who ran or read the strips; 'read at the drug-checking sites' would match it. (Revised in step 2: my blind note also questioned 'held only these'; on re-checking, the Table 3 note itself says the six held only typical benzodiazepines, so the claim follows the paper.)
claims.note: Every Laing number in the statement and magnitude recomputes from Table 3 and the p. 6 text: 15/24 = 62.5% (Wilson 42.7-78.8, same), FNR 9/24 = 37.5%; 20/129 = 15.5% (Wilson 10.3-22.7, same), specificity 109/129 = 84.5% (Wilson 77.3-89.7); 7/8 = 87.5% and 8/16 = 50.0% (Wilson 28.0-72.0, same), both also re-counted sample by sample from Table 2; FTIR 2/24 (FNR 22/24 = 91.7%), FPR 5/129 = 3.9%; either method 17/24 detected, 23 false positives (23/129 = 17.8%, FNR 7/24 = 29.2%); 1368 and 159; 2 of 7 at both laboratories; 17 of 24 with fentanyl. That all six typical-benzodiazepine samples were strip-positive follows from Table 1 (41 strip positives of 159) minus Table 3 (35 of 153); the text says only 'each detected by test strips'. Conditions the claim does not state: the dilution (2-3 mg dissolved in an unstated volume of water; not reported), the reading rule (not described), the manufacturer's urine cut-off (oxazepam calibrator, 300 ng/mL; reported on p. 2), that the strip was read after the FTIR result with one combined result recorded (index test not read blind to FTIR), and that the reference was positive if any NPS benzodiazepine appeared in one or more of GC-MS, LC-MS or qNMR at either laboratory (Table 1 footnote). The accuracy subset came from five of the eight sites (p. 3). The paper also relays a laboratory report by the same group (Shapiro et al., 2020; pp. 2-3) in which similar benzodiazepine strips detected etizolam, at a higher minimum concentration than flualprazolam and flubromazolam; with Laing's own 8 of 16 etizolam-only positives this sits against the claim's Sisco 2024b sentence that the strip did not react to etizolam at any concentration tried, and the claim should say the sources disagree (different strip lots or test conditions are possible; not established). What the 20 false-positive samples contained is indeed not reported (Tables 1 and 2 imply most were samples expected to be fentanyl, an inference only).

anchors.extracted: Benzodiazepine strip testing ran from October 2018 to January 2020 at eight harm-reduction sites in Vancouver and Surrey; samples for confirmatory testing were sent from five of them (3 Vancouver, 2 Surrey); data were collected anonymously.

Point-of-care testing in two steps: 2-3 mg of the sample analysed by FTIR, then dissolved in water (volume not given), strip added, one combined result recorded. Confirmatory samples were a convenience subset: discarded or unreclaimed samples, clients asking for further analysis, or clinical suspicion of benzodiazepine overdose; the laboratory (PTC or DAS) depended on availability or site. Seven NPS-benzodiazepine samples went to both laboratories: 5 (71.4%) confirmed at both, 2 (28.6%) at only one.

BTNX Rapid Response single-drug benzodiazepine strip: product insert gives an oxazepam calibrator, cut-off 300 ng/mL, validated for 22 benzodiazepines in urine; the authors note the strips were not designed for dissolved drug samples. They relay a laboratory report (Shapiro et al., 2020) in which flualprazolam and flubromazolam were detected at concentrations similar to alprazolam and etizolam at a higher minimum concentration judged still useful for drug checking, with no cross-reaction with fentanyl.

1368 samples were checked with both benzodiazepine strips and FTIR (1379 strip-tested, 11 without FTIR, out of 6156 submitted); 159 of them also had confirmatory testing (120 at DAS, 65 at PTC, 26 at both). Fig. 1 lists the reasons for confirmatory selection, including clinical suspicion of benzodiazepine overdose or toxicity.

anchors.locator: Results > Point-of-care accuracy & error, 1st-2nd paragraphs; Table 3
anchors.extracted: Six of 159 samples held typical benzodiazepines (alprazolam, temazepam) and no NPS benzodiazepine, were strip-detected and were removed, leaving 153. Strips: 35 positive (15 confirmed NPS benzodiazepine, 20 not), 118 negative (9 confirmed, 109 not). FTIR: 7 positive (2 confirmed, 5 not), 146 negative (22 confirmed, 124 not). Both positive 2 (0 confirmed); either positive 40 (17 confirmed, 23 not; FPR 17.8%); both negative 113 (7 confirmed; FNR 29.2%). Editors' recomputation: strip sensitivity 15/24 = 62.5% (Wilson 42.7-78.8), false positives 20/129 = 15.5% (10.3-22.7), specificity 84.5%.

anchors.locator: Results > Point-of-care accuracy & error, 3rd-4th paragraphs; Table 2 (p. 5)
anchors.extracted: Strips detected 62.5% (15/24) of confirmed NPS-benzodiazepine samples: 87.5% (n = 8) when flualprazolam, flubromazolam or flubromazepam was present, 50.0% (n = 16) with etizolam only (re-counted from Table 2: 7/8 and 8/16). Strip FPR 15.5%, FNR 37.5%. FTIR: 5 of 7 positives not confirmed (FPR 3.9%), 22 of 146 negatives confirmed (FNR 91.7%); FTIR found the 2 etizolam samples that strips missed.

anchors.locator: Results > NPS benzodiazepines in primary sample, 1st paragraph; NPS benzodiazepines and opioids, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: 24 of 159 (15.1%) contained an NPS benzodiazepine, none expected as such (expected fentanyl 15, alprazolam 5, 'down' 2, heroin 1, unknown 1); 17 of the 24 also contained an opioid, always fentanyl (one also carfentanil); printed 70.1%, but 17/24 = 70.8%.

Strips are made for urine metabolites of common benzodiazepines (oxazepam, nordiazepam) and may give false negatives with NPS benzodiazepines or diluted drug samples; etizolam is reportedly insoluble in water and others needed sonication and vortexing to dissolve these NPS benzodiazepines; FTIR detects small quantities in mixtures poorly; small subsamples may under- or overestimate the error rates; the newest compounds may escape targeted confirmatory assays; voluntary drug checking may not represent the wider market.

Reference standard: positive if any NPS benzodiazepine was found by one or more of GC-MS, LC-MS and qNMR. The strip footnote says strips may detect NPS and non-NPS benzodiazepines. The composition of the 20 strip-positive, NPS-negative samples is not reported.

claims.note: Editors' count from Table 2 reproduced: of the 17 fentanyl-containing NPS-benzodiazepine samples, FTIR listed fentanyl in 3 (samples 6 and 19 'fentanyl', sample 20 'fentanyl or analog'; 2 of 17 if 'or analog' is not counted), and named an NPS benzodiazepine (etizolam) in 2 of 24 (samples 1-2). 24/159 = 15.1% and 17/24 recompute (the paper prints 70.1% for 17/24, which is 70.8%). The point-of-care service also used fentanyl test strips (p. 2), whose results for these samples are not reported, so the FTIR count describes FTIR alone, as the claim says, not the whole service. Laing measured no amounts.

anchors.extracted: 24 of 159 samples (15.1%) held an NPS benzodiazepine on confirmatory testing and none was expected by the person to contain one; 15 were expected to be fentanyl.

anchors.extracted: 17 of the 24 also contained an opioid, always fentanyl (one also carfentanil); printed as 70.1% (17/24 = 70.8%).

Per sample, FTIR versus confirmatory analysis: FTIR most often listed only caffeine, while the laboratories found up to five components (e.g. fentanyl, etizolam, phenacetin, methamphetamine, 4-ANPP); FTIR listed fentanyl in 3 of the 17 fentanyl-containing samples and etizolam in 2 of 24.

FTIR has a documented limitation for low-concentration components, particularly in mixtures; fentanyl test strips were used alongside FTIR at point of care, but their results for these samples are not given.

key_findings.correction: Counts match Fig. 1 and the text; the 542 versus 543 gap is real.
The 7 of 8 and 8 of 16 were also re-counted sample by sample from Table 2; Wilson intervals in the card's analysis field (42.7-78.8, 10.3-22.7, 28.0-72.0) reproduce.
All five counts re-derived from Table 2: caffeine 19/19, fentanyl 3/17 (counting sample 20's 'fentanyl or analog'), methamphetamine 1/10, phenacetin 0/7, NPS benzodiazepine 2/24.
The relayed report also judged etizolam's higher minimum detectable concentration still within a useful range for drug checking (p. 3).

risk_of_bias.note: Agree with overall high. JBI-prevalence fits the first aim (which NPS benzodiazepines were found), but cl_dc_benzo_strips rests on the second aim, strips and FTIR against laboratory analysis of the same samples, which is the test-accuracy design of METHODS 0.3.1, so an adjudicator may want QUADAS-2 for that aim. My QUADAS-2 judgments: sample selection high (convenience subset, partly sent because of suspected benzodiazepine overdose or at the client's request, possibly after seeing the point-of-care result; 6 typical-benzodiazepine samples removed after testing); index test high (off-label on dissolved drug of unreported concentration; strip read after FTIR with one combined result recorded; reading rule and reader not reported); reference standard high (two laboratories with different targeted methods chosen by availability or site, 2 of 7 duplicates discordant, any-positive composite, newest compounds may be missed, blinding to point-of-care results not reported); flow and timing high (159 of 1368 verified, non-randomly; reference differed by laboratory; interval not reported). Overall high, the same as the card.

missed: p. 3, Methods 2nd paragraph: FTIR was run first and the strip then read with one combined result recorded, so the strip reading was not blind to FTIR, and who read the strips is not stated; the card's assessor-blinding field says only 'not reported'.
p. 3, Methods 5th paragraph: confirmatory samples came from five of the eight sites (3 Vancouver, 2 Surrey), so the accuracy figures describe five sites.

p. 3, Methods 2nd paragraph: the amount tested (2-3 mg per sample, analysed by FTIR before dissolving in water) is reported, though the water volume is not; useful beside the card's note that dissolution is unreported.
